title: VLA-Retain: Benchmarking Cross-Dimension Effects of Vision Tuning in VLAs
abstract: arXiv:2610.27698v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models transfer knowledge from large-scale pretraining into robot control, but their manipulation performance remains sensitive to changes in observation conditions, which recent work addresses by fine-tuning the visual module on target-domain data. However, it remains unclear how such adaptation affects robustness beyond the target condition, as existing robustness benchmarks only evaluate models without fine-tuning and adaptation studies only report the target gain. Measuring this cross-dimension effect requires separating target gains from off-target changes, isolating adaptation effects from architectural differences, ruling out generic forgetting, and comparing tuning choices. Therefore, we introduce VLA-Retain, a benchmark that compares five open VLA models, tuned on Camera-view or Sensor-noise data, with their own base checkpoints on LIBERO-Plus dataset spanning seven perturbation dimensions. translated_title: VLA-Retain：VLA模型中视觉微调跨维度效应的基准测试
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言-动作模型将大规模预训练中习得的知识迁移到机器人控制中，但其操作性能对观测条件的变化仍然敏感，近期的工作通过在目标域数据上微调视觉模块来应对这一问题。然而，这种适配如何影响目标条件之外的鲁棒性仍不清楚，因为现有的鲁棒性基准只在未微调的模型上进行评估，而适配研究仅报告目标条件上的增益。测量这种跨维度效应需要将目标增益与目标外的变化分离开来，将适配效应与架构差异隔离开来，排除一般性遗忘的干扰，并比较不同的微调选择。因此，我们提出了VLA-Retain，这是一个基准测试，在跨越七个扰动维度的LIBERO-Plus数据集上，将五个分别在相机视角或传感器噪声数据上微调的开源VLA模型与其各自的基础检查点进行比较。我们的研究……
tldr: 该论文提出VLA-Retain基准，通过在七个扰动维度上比较五个经视觉微调的开源VLA模型与其原始检查点，首次系统评估了视觉微调对模型在目标条件之外鲁棒性的跨维度影响。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces VLA-Retain, a benchmark that for the first time systematically measures the cross-dimension effects of vision tuning on VLA robustness by comparing five fine-tuned open VLA models against their base checkpoints across seven perturbation dimensions of LIBERO-Plus.
